* How important is Zoe Quinn's affair with Eron Gjoni to you? And how important to GamerGate at-large?

[Discussion] What is GamerGate about to you?

What is GamerGate in your eyes?

A pushback against corruption, censorship and political extremists in the gaming industry.

How important is ethics in gaming journalism to you? And how important to GamerGate at-large?

3 and 3. I support ethics in gaming journalism, but it's not a major issue for me. I enjoy discussing journalistic ethics with people, but am not an avid reader of games journalism or have much stake in it. I do think it's important that we build a gaming media that is ethical and responsible though.

How important is opposing anti-consumer practices to you? And how important to GamerGate at-large?

4 and 3. I would like to see more focus on industry issues within GamerGate.

How important is creative freedom to you? And how important to GamerGate at-large?

5 and 5. One of the main reasons I got involved with GamerGate in the first place.

How important is free speech to you? And how important to GamerGate at-large?

I thought it would be interesting to have a discussion on why people got involved with GamerGate.

**Discussion Questions**

* When did you get involved in the controversy?

* Why did you get involved with supporting GamerGate?

* Have your views on GamerGate and/or the gaming community changed since your involvement?

* Have your views on social justice and/or feminism changed since your involvement?

* Do you think the GamerGate community is a force for good in the gaming industry?
Why did you get involved with GamerGate?

When did you get involved in the controversy?

Around March 2015.

Why did you get involved with supporting or opposing GamerGate?

I saw Internet Aristocrat's videos on GamerGate and decided to check it out on Twitter. I started off pretty neutral and tried talking to people on both sides, but it quickly became apparent which side was right. The pro-GamerGate side was nothing but friendly, backed up everything with sources and was more than happy to engaged in a dialogue. The anti-GamerGate side blocked me and at times disrespected me just for asking for evidence. After countless interactions with both sides, I began to lean heavily pro-GG.

What really convinced me to fully support GamerGate though was when I saw social justice warriors attacking game developers and comic book artists, demanding that they change their artistic vision to suit their political agenda. I also saw plenty of GamerGate people being attacked by hypocritical "anti-harassment" activists, who did nothing but lie about people for money and engage in behavior far worse than most GamerGate people would ever even consider engaging in. I knew I had to do the right thing and stand up for GamerGate and for gamers

Have your views on GamerGate and/or the gaming community changed since your involvement?

I've really come to appreciate gaming and the gaming community a lot more since I got involved with GamerGate. I've also become a lot more moderate in my pro-GamerGate stances since I first got involved with the controversy.

Have your views on social justice and/or feminism changed since your involvement?

I've become a lot more antagonistic towards the social justice community, many of their ideas and feminsm in general since being involved. I have, however, become much more open minded when it comes to dealing with people of different political views, as GamerGate is a bipartisan cause composed of both liberals and conservatives. I have also become more accepting of trans people as a result of my involvement in GamerGate.

Do you think the GamerGate community is a force for good in the gaming industry?

Absolutely.

When did you get involved in the controversy?

A few months after GG began, I can't remember the exact time.

Why did you get involved with supporting GamerGate?

I was just lurking the KiA subreddit at the time.

Have your views on GamerGate and/or the gaming community changed since your involvement?

Before I realized the insanity and evils of Social Justice, I thought GG was stupid and blown out of proportion. I thought both sides, GG and aGG, just needed to calm down.

Have your views on social justice and/or feminism changed since your involvement?

I had thought that feminism and SocJus were hip and progressive. I now see those movements as hollow, regressive, and destructive. I am greatful that GG helped me open my eyes.

Do you think the GamerGate community is a force for good in the gaming industry?

I see it as a force for good in society, culture, and politics, not just gaming.

When did you get involved in the controversy?

At the start.

Why did you get involved with supporting GamerGate?

There was an uproar of people pissed off about corruption in games journalism. I though to myself "It is about damn time. If they are actually going to do something about this, then I am in like Flynn."

Have your views on GamerGate and/or the gaming community changed since your involvement?

Not much.

Have your views on social justice and/or feminism changed since your involvement?

My overall opinion has moved to having a much lower opinion of those two movements. It is also a more refined view, where I recognize that there are people who call themselves feminists that do good work towards equality, and there are good people who work towards social justice. But there are the people actually doing work, not whining about their first world problems on twitter.

Do you think the GamerGate community is a force for good in the gaming industry?

Yes. Promoting ethical games journalism. Also some game makers are starting to self-censor games, and this is one of the few ways to hold back the wave of unnecessary censorship.

I'd heard about it on a message board for an MMO from uninformed SEA people, but they made the GG controversy sound dumb and boring. Then, I lost my job and felt the need to waste time on YouTube, so I started browsing for content and found Sargon of Akkad.

When did you get involved in the controversy?

I was late to the party, about June 2015.

Why did you get involved with supporting GamerGate?

I had given up on games journalism back in the early 2000's due to review scores being wildly unrepresentative of my experience (I actually thought I was just weird and wanted different things from games than most others). I had been driven mad by SJW tactics and theories invading politics, sports and academia. I stumbled across an Anita video then went down the rabbit hole from there.

Have your views on GamerGate and/or the gaming community changed since your involvement?

Yes, before I would have hesitated to call myself a gamer. I play mostly strategy and the odd RPG; I don't like co-op games or FPS and so I didn't think I was a "real" gamer. Now I proudly wear the title that 1000+ hours of EU IV means I deserve. I never used to interact with other gamers socially (except my irl friends) and so gamergate has nudged me into a more active role within the community.

Have your views on social justice and/or feminism changed since your involvement?

Nah, they changed significantly a few years before. Though I guess I think even less of SJW's now, I didn't realise quite how many of them were bullies and abusers.

Do you think the GamerGate community is a force for good in the gaming industry?

Yes.

When did you get involved in the controversy?

Early 2015 iirc, heard about it on DramaAlert

Why did you get involved with supporting GamerGate?

Because corruption and lying is immoral and wrong.

Have your views on GamerGate and/or the gaming community changed since your involvement?

Nope.

Have your views on social justice and/or feminism changed since your involvement?

Yeah, I would call myself a feminist before I started getting involved in GamerGate.

Do you think the GamerGate community is a force for good in the gaming industry?

Yep, we've done some pretty impressive stuff imo, like SPJ airplay.

When did you get involved in the controversy?

August 2014, back when Gamergate was still referred to as The Quinnspiracy/Five Guys Burgers and Fries.

Why did you get involved with supporting GamerGate?

It all started so long ago, that it's rough to pinpoint my original reasoning. At this point, however, it's about weakening, if not eliminating the power structure in the games industry that pushes people with the "right" viewpoints further in the industry, while attempting to keep people with the "wrong" viewpoints out of the industry. The fact that I've seen people involved in the industry that I've known for years be silent about, if not flat-out condone this system has only furthered my determination in doing something about it.

Have your views on GamerGate and/or the gaming community changed since your involvement?

I've become much more respectful of the gaming community, while becoming more cynical towards a number of developers (particularly due to IGDA-related incidents). I've once again become quite fine with the "gamer" label, and have become more open to discussing development decisions with the community at large.

Have your views on social justice and/or feminism changed since your involvement?

I had a disdain for the social justice community well before Gamergate started, and the events that occurred both in and out of Gamergate have put an exclamation point on said disdain. There are still good people within that community, though, who just happened to fall into the wrong group of friends. I legitimately feel bad for them, and hopefully they'll have more moderate positions down the road, if anything. As for feminism, believe it or not, I've gained some respect for it. At least for the ones that ACTUALLY care about equality, and don't just want to pretty much control society.

Do you think the GamerGate community is a force for good in the gaming industry?

In spite of all of the split opinions that have formed over time in GG, causing a fair share of infighting, I'm absolutely convinced that Gamergate is a force for good. Gamergate's very existence has forced things to be discussed that would have otherwise never been touched, even if some of those things are sadly still being just handwaved. Stuff like the unhealthy relationship between devs and journos, the blatant bias favoring devs who think a certain way, censorship disguised as localization, and the general shilling of games without disclosure of financial/social connections are absolutely important issues that need to be talked about on an industry-wide level, and hopefully as time goes on, we'll see more of that. Although it will mostly likely require for more politically-neutral dev organizations to start gaining more traction.

When did you get involved in the controversy?

August 2014, when the ZoePost hit.

Why did you get involved with supporting GamerGate?

A friend of mine from my local Atheist/Skeptic group had roused the ire of the SJW's by "doxxing" a Skepchick business owner (rhymes with Squirrely Lamey Broth). He lost a shot at being a Secular Council for America state leader on the basis of her and her fellow SJW's petitioning for him to not get the job. Granted, he stepped aside, but that's how the A/S community worked before Gamergate - way too much fucking capitulation to these fucks because we didn't want to be perceived as misogynists or racists (doesn't help that 75% of us are older white dudes).

And then GamerGate happened and a diverse community fought back, ready to wage (and continue waging) a long, arduous war against these corrupt, unethical bastards who have demonized several once-decent ideologies with their constant claims of victimhood. I couldn't stand by and grit my teeth this time, so I grabbed a bucket of lube and hopped on board the love train.

Have your views on GamerGate and/or the gaming community changed since your involvement?

Nope, I always pegged us for a diverse bunch of nuts who enjoyed games. I grew up in the 80's and saw everybody go crazy over arcade games, regardless of race/gender/religion/economic status/position on pineapple on pizza. I was pleasantly surprised though to see such delicious backlash against the ideologues peddling horseshit whilst pimping their Patreons.

Have your views on social justice and/or feminism changed since your involvement?

No. I'd seen Atheism + born, I'd seen the bullshit from Free(from)ThoughtBlogs and the crazy that the SJW's brought to the Atheism/Skeptic community.

Do you think the GamerGate community is a force for good in the gaming industry?

Gawker is dying, the industry has repeatedly supported ethics, and regular folks are finally seeing the batshit crazy of the radfem crybullies and intersectional oppression olympians. So yeah, we done good, and I've no doubt we'll all keep our eyes out to call shenanigans on the shysters and swindlers masquerading as pop culture experts.

When did you get involved in the controversy?

I was in as soon as I heard about it. As soon as 5 guys hit, and I saw the hysterical reactions to something that could have easily been solved by 1.) Grayson just saying "oops, here's let me amend the article I wrote about Quinn's game," and 2.) letting it fizzle itself out. I knew we had reached a breaking point. It was time to address some personalities that were doing some dubious shit.

Why did you get involved with supporting GamerGate?

I saw the rise of A+. I knew I had to do...something...

Have your views on GamerGate and/or the gaming community changed since your involvement?

When I began, I was more hardcore "ethics only." Now I think GamerGate should be "mostly ethics, but let's also keep an eye on certain reoccurring personalities in problem children." So I've kind of a little changed my view on GamerGate, but not too much. The gaming community is the gaming community. We're going to argue over whose console is better, PC gamers with mid tier PCs will feel smug and superior, and we'll all ask Capcom why they're not going to make a Dragon's Dogma sequel with all our hearts regardless of what else is going on.

Have your views on social justice and/or feminism changed since your involvement?

I view feminism specifically a little more kindly than I used to. Feminists, you can thank Based Mom for that.

Do you think the GamerGate community is a force for good in the gaming industry?

Hell, I think it's been a force of good in just my life. I'm now a much more informed consumer of all media, which can do nothing but improve my life.
